newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Over 1,000 compete for Albania parliament seats.
newsitem.headline: Over 1,000 compete for Albania parliament seats.

text.p: Albania's parliamentary elections, called early to end months of instability, will be conducted in two rounds, the first on Sunday and the second round on July 6.
The first will be combined with a referendum on whether to restore the monarchy, which ruled for ten years before King Zog fled the country after Italian troops invaded in April 1939.

Some 4,525 polling stations across the mountainous Balkan nation will open at 8 a.m. (0600 GMT). The constitutional court has yet to decide whether they will close earlier than the originally planned 9 p.m. (1700 GMT).

Political parties and the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), which is overseeing the vote, want polls to close at 6 p.m. to ensure the safety of voters and hundreds of international observers across the country.
Almost 2.065 million elegible voters will elect 155 members of parliament for a four-year term, out of 1,112 candidates.
Of the total seats, 115 will be allocated on a first-past-the-post basis.
If a candidate fails to win more than 50 percent of the vote in the first round, there will be a run-off between the leading two candidates on July 6.
The remaining 40 seats will be allocated according to the overall share of the vote one party gets, but only among those parties that win more than two percent of valid votes.
A total of 27 political parties will be fighting for seats in the one-chamber People's Assembly.
Eight of the parties have fielded candidates in fewer than 25 constituencies and therefore are eligible under election rules to compete only for the 115 seats allocated by the majority system.

Final official results will be issued by the Central Electoral Commission, which has 17 members representing the 10 parties which formed a broad-based interim government to prepare the snap poll and re-establish order in the country.
The OSCE is expected to give an early verdict on the poll by late Monday and first results could come out a day later.
